clauses.reason: Section 1 designates and empowers the Secretary of State to perform, without the approval, ratification or other action of the President, the Article IV function of determining by common agreement with the President of Mexico other species of birds to be added to the Convention list. It is a standing delegation with no end term, and nothing held changes it.

research_rationale:
EO 11629 (signed October 26, 1971; 36 FR 20647, Federal Register issue of October 28, 1971) delegates to the Secretary of State the function vested in the President by Article IV of the Convention between the United States and Mexico for the Protection of Migratory Birds and Game Mammals (50 Stat. 1311; TS 912) to determine, by common agreement with the President of Mexico, other species of birds to be added to the list of protected migratory birds, and requires the Secretary of State to consult the Secretary of the Interior. I read the complete held Federal Register text: the title, an authority paragraph, section 1 (the delegation), section 2 (the consultation duty) and the signature. The dossier inventory of two clauses covers sections 1 and 2 and I confirmed it without correction. The order has no end date or ending condition and revokes nothing. The held-text number search finds EO 11629 only in the 1989 OFR codification snapshot (historical editorial, not a current basis) and in a second held copy of the order itself; none of the three selected searches (U.S. Code through 2026-10-09, eCFR as of 2026-10-14, Federal Register executive-order catalog disposition notes) has a hit, and none records an amendment, revocation or supersession. I do not hold the Convention text or evidence about its present status; the claim rests on the absence of any held ending instrument for a standing delegation and asserts nothing about the Convention beyond what the order recites. Both clauses are operative on the original text, checked through 2026-10-14.
